Build a linking-review synthesis object

Source: R/api-advanced.R, R/help_linking_and_dff.R
build_linking_review.Rd

Build a linking-review synthesis object

Usage

build_linking_review(
  anchor_review = NULL,
  drift = NULL,
  chain = NULL,
  top_n = 10
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_linking_review'
summary(object, digits = 3, top_n = 10, ...)

Arguments

anchor_review

Optional output from review_mfrm_anchors().

drift

Optional output from detect_anchor_drift().

chain

Optional output from build_equating_chain().

top_n

For build_linking_review(): Maximum number of linking-risk rows to highlight in summary outputs. The full object keeps the full risk tables.

For summary(): Number of top linking-risk rows to keep in the compact summary.

object

Output from build_linking_review().

digits

Number of digits for printed numeric values.

...

Reserved for generic compatibility.

Value

An object of class mfrm_linking_review.

For summary(): An object of class summary.mfrm_linking_review.

Details

Combine saved anchor, drift and chain results without recalculation. Choose the inputs for the question: review_mfrm_anchors() checks receiving-data constraints, detect_anchor_drift() compares waves with a reference, and build_equating_chain() follows adjacent links. These are complementary sources, not a required sequence.

The combined review does not verify source-fit readiness, cross-wave identity, invariance or group-anchor assumptions, and cannot establish scale equivalence or score comparability. Its documented scope is RSM/PCM; GPCM drift/chain inputs remain exploratory with scope supported_with_caveat.

summary() method: Summarize a linking-review object

Using the review

Read overview for supplied sources and status, then top_linking_risks for ranked follow-up. group_view_index groups by wave, link, facet or source family. plot_map routes to the source plots; reporting_map identifies coverage and separate manuscript-reporting helpers. Retain the original results when inspecting risks or deciding next actions.

Linking and DFF route map

QuestionRoute
Do planned/observed assignments connect ratings?describe_mfrm_data() (design_connectivity), subset_connectivity_report()
Which baseline locations can serve as anchors?make_anchor_table(), review_mfrm_anchors()
How do I fit new data with baseline locations fixed?anchor_to_baseline()
Have common elements shifted across waves?detect_anchor_drift(), build_equating_chain(), build_linking_review()
Do facet levels differ between groups?analyze_dff() (mfrm_report(x, type = "dff")); see mantel_haenszel_table() and ordinal_logistic_table()

Keep four concepts distinct: common ratings (observed overlap), scale identification (e.g., sum-to-zero centering), direct anchors (Facet, Level, Anchor fixing internal logit coordinates), and group anchors (Facet, Level, Group, GroupValue fixing an unweighted arithmetic group mean). With centering_scope = "facet" (default), centered facets sum to zero across all levels including anchors/groups; "remainder" centers unconstrained levels only; "anchor_origin" (additive RSM/PCM JML) lets anchors replace centering on their facet when an active unanchored noncenter_facet is selected.

detect_anchor_drift() and build_equating_chain() estimate one pooled offset per link (Offset_SD is residual spread across retained elements, not an offset SE; LinkSupportAdequate is a local 5-element count screen, not proof of invariance). Source-anchor covariance is excluded unless explicitly requested via anchor_covariance and independent_anchors = TRUE in mfrm_facet_intervals() (intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin MML).

See also

review_mfrm_anchors(), detect_anchor_drift(), build_equating_chain(), plot(x), mfrmr_linking_and_dff

build_linking_review()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("build_linking_review", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Deliberately linked teaching waves: common labels below represent the
# same rater and criterion identities by construction.
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
people <- unique(toy$Person)
# Two balanced 24-Person waves retain every Rater and Criterion.
d1 <- toy[toy$Person %in% people[1:24], , drop = FALSE]
d2 <- toy[toy$Person %in% people[25:48], , drop = FALSE]
fit1 <- fit_mfrm(d1, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 method = "MML", quad_points = 7, maxit = 30)
fit2 <- fit_mfrm(d2, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 method = "MML", quad_points = 7, maxit = 30)
anchor_review_obj <- review_mfrm_anchors(d1, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score")
drift <- detect_anchor_drift(list(Wave1 = fit1, Wave2 = fit2))
chain <- build_equating_chain(list(Wave1 = fit1, Wave2 = fit2))
review <- build_linking_review(anchor_review = anchor_review_obj, drift = drift, chain = chain)
summary(review)
review$top_linking_risks
review$group_view_index
} # }
